title: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
seo_title: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Class 12 Chemistry Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_code: Class 12 Chemistry, Chapter 7: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
standard_text: Alcohols: nomenclature, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties (of primary alcohols only), identification of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols, mechanism of dehydration. Phenols: nomenclature, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties, acidic nature of phenol, electrophilic substitution reactions, uses of phenols. Ethers: nomenclature, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties, uses.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: classifying and naming alcohols, preparation, oxidation, acidity of phenols, named reactions and ethers. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Phenol is more acidic than alcohols.
body_html:
How to think about it

Alcohols are 1°, 2° or 3° by the carbon bearing –OH; they hydrogen-bond, so they boil higher than ethers and alkanes of similar mass. Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes (PCC) and acids; secondary to ketones; tertiary resist oxidation. The Lucas test tells them apart.

Phenols are more acidic than alcohols because the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised; –NO₂ groups make them stronger. The –OH group activates the ring for bromination, nitration, the Reimer–Tiemann and Kolbe reactions. Ethers are made by the Williamson synthesis and cleaved by HI.

Example

Propan-2-ol is?

–OH on a C with two C

Answer: secondary

Example

Phenol + bromine water?

tribromination

Answer: 2,4,6-tribromophenol

Common mistakes

  • Saying ethanol is more acidic than phenol.
  • Oxidising a 3° alcohol to a ketone.
  • Breaking the O–aryl bond in anisole with HI.

faq.q: Why is phenol more acidic than ethanol?
faq.a: The negative charge of the phenoxide ion is delocalised over the benzene ring, stabilising it.

faq.q: How does the Lucas test distinguish alcohols?
faq.a: Tertiary alcohols turn cloudy at once, secondary in about five minutes, primary not at room temperature.
